chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Eating walnuts during intense heat agitates the heat in the body cavity and agitates sores on the body, and eating it in winter warms the kidneys and dispels the cold.'
ai.seo_question: What are the health benefits and drawbacks of eating walnuts in different seasons according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ali (AS), recorded in Al-Kafi, reflects the Shia tradition of integrating practical medicine (Tibb) with spiritual wisdom, emphasizing the concept of 'temperament' (Mizaj) in dietary habits. It highlights the prophetic tradition of aligning food consumption with seasonal changes to maintain bodily balance, specifically noting how walnuts' warming nature benefits the kidneys in winter but may exacerbate heat-related ailments in summer.
